memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not spread false reports. Do not help a guilty person by being a malicious witness." - Exodus 23:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins this section by guarding something we often treat far too lightly: our words about other people. He forbids spreading false reports and lending our voice to lies that harm the innocent. In the ancient courtroom, a false witness could destroy a person's life. But even outside a court, a rumour passed along, a story twisted, a reputation quietly damaged — these do real harm. God takes the truth of our speech seriously.

How easily we become carriers of things we never verified. Someone tells us a juicy piece of news, and without a second thought we pass it on. We share the message, forward the story, repeat the gossip. But God calls His people to be different — to refuse to spread what may be false, and never to lend our voice to what harms another unjustly. Truth is not just about not lying outright; it is about not carelessly passing on damage.

Jesus is called the truth itself (John 14:6), and those who follow Him are meant to be people of truth in a world drowning in falsehood. Before we speak or share, it is worth asking: Is this true? Is it fair? Could this harm someone unjustly? May God make us trustworthy with our words, people whose speech builds up rather than tears down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I verify things before passing them on, or spread reports carelessly?
Have my words ever unjustly damaged someone's reputation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me a person of truth in a world full of falsehood. Guard my tongue from spreading what is false or harmful, and let my words build others up. Amen.
